speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a fever and altered mental status starting two days ago; to help me understand your condition, have you experienced any seizures, headaches, or neck stiffness?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome (NMS). The clinical picture of fever and altered mentation in a patient on haloperidol with a history of tics is highly suggestive of NMS, especially given the absence of other infectious or inflammatory symptoms.
